partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community events, and member programs. The Guild provides hands-on classes, special interest groups, and resources to support woodworkers of all skill levels in the Kansas City area.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community events, and member programs. The Guild provides hands-on classes, special interest groups, and resources to support woodworkers of all skill levels in the Kansas City area.

programServices.description: Landscaping and horticultural services including installation of fountains and garden lighting, plants and soil, sprinkler and drip systems, labor for installation and maintenance, pest control, and related job materials. The Guild provided these program services to members and the public as part of its hands-on vocational and craft education mission.

Equipment maintenance and repair services, including equipment repairs and general maintenance, supporting the Guild's workshop operations and member access to tools and machinery used in woodworking education and craft programs.

Membership programs and event registrations administered through WildApricot, including monthly membership meetings, Rough to Ready workshops, special interest groups (SIGs) in laser engraving, finishing, carving, hand tools, and CNC, and woodworking classes such as Basic Woodworking, Intermediate Woodworking, Bandsaw Box, and Intro to Hand Tool Woodworking.

line4d_otherProgramServices.description: No other program services to report.

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization incorporated in Missouri in 1992. Its mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, community engagement, and member support. The Guild offers hands-on woodworking classes (including Basic Woodworking, Intermediate Woodworking, Bandsaw Box, and Intro to Hand Tool Woodworking), monthly membership meetings, Rough to Ready workshops, and special interest groups (SIGs) covering laser engraving, finishing, carving, hand tools, and CNC. The Guild also provides landscaping and horticultural program services, design services, and product sales as part of its vocational craft education activities.

The Form 990 was prepared by the organization's treasurer and bookkeeper using QuickBooks and WildApricot financial records. A copy of the completed Form 990 was provided to all members of the governing body for review prior to filing. No formal written review process policy exists; review is conducted informally by the Treasurer and available board members.

The organization makes its governing documents and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization does not currently post these documents on a public website. No formal conflict of interest policy is in place as of the tax year end.

The opening balance equity of -$9,337.50 per QuickBooks represents accumulated deficits from prior periods not previously reported on Form 990.

The organization owns a truck recorded at original cost of $13,495.00 on the balance sheet (Part X, Line 10a). No accumulated depreciation has been recorded in QuickBooks as of the tax year end. The truck is used in connection with the organization's landscaping and program service activities.

Other liabilities reported on Part X, Line 25 ($370.94) consist of Board of Equalization Payable ($370.94) and Arizona Department of Revenue Payable ($0.00) as reported in QuickBooks. These represent sales tax liabilities accrued in connection with the organization's product sales and service activities.
